//: Workload for the mcpdemo config (hotel schema). Weights are relative, not percentages.
//why: Every entry binds a VARYING value. A hundred thousand calls binding one literal
//why2: measures Oracle's cursor cache, not the server -- a real, repeatable figure
//why3: describing a workload nobody has. ${random:a-b} and ${seq} exist for that.

tools.//: The correctness check, not a throughput entry. Every value must differ AND the
tools.//2: values must span exactly as many numbers as there were calls -- which is what
tools.//3: proves each call reached Oracle rather than a cache, a retry or a shared result.
tools.//4: A throughput figure alone cannot tell a fast server from a broken one.

tools.//: Two parameterless SELECTs: the cheapest real round trip in this schema, so they
tools.//2: set the floor the heavier entries are read against.

tools.//: A primary-key fetch across the REAL key range of this table (1-7 today), so every
tools.//2: call returns a row. A range wider than the data would still be a valid load -- a
tools.//3: miss is a full round trip and an index probe -- but it would quietly measure the
tools.//4: not-found path instead of the fetch. What it must never be is the SAME key each
tools.//5: time: that measures Oracle cursor cache, not this server.
